## 9. Backward audit: the adversity assumed in correcting concern

6 October 2026. AI-authored continuation of the [whole-process inquiry](../../../../theories/shengsheng-buxi-generative-existence/unified-2026-10-05/UNIFIED-ETHICAL-GROUNDING.md#when-fulfilled-concern-itself-needs-correction). The named connection is **actual unwanted undergoing → local adversity → a ground for correcting a formed orientation**. This audits a dependence of the correction argument; it does not replace whole-process grounding with an independently supplied patient ontology.

The [concern-object argument](WHOLE-PROCESS-REALIZATION-ARGUMENT.md#10-concerns-object-and-the-grounds-of-its-correction) proposes a defect in welcoming an occurrence precisely because it is adverse. That proposal already uses the occurrence's independently warranted adversity. Running the explanation backward—welcoming this is defective, therefore undergoing it is bad—would recycle that input. Independently justified evidence about fitting attitudes could support an account of value; the present argument has not supplied such independent justification. Neither the occurrence of an attitude nor a proposed rule about its fittingness closes the dependence.

The restricted domain in §2 must therefore keep three senses of “unwanted” distinct. **Constitutive experiential opposition** describes the manner of undergoing. **A further rejecting attitude** concerns one's response to that experience. **Warranted rejection** already claims evaluative justification. The candidate intends the first, without requiring the second or building in the third. Calling an experience negative does not establish its bad-for quality. Conversely, substituting a separate preference for the complete experiential mode would change the target. Whether that mode concerns a bodily condition or the experience itself also remains substantive; opposition cannot simply be translated into a command to eliminate its own occurrence.

The [new Massin comparison](AFFECTIVE-REALIZATION-SOURCES.md#massin-an-identity-with-a-different-bearer) gives an explicit identity account whose value bearer is a bodily episode. His distinction allows genuine suffering of an apparent pain while its bodily object is absent. Consequently, importing that identity would leave our question about the undergoing itself unanswered. This is neither a denial of experiential adversity nor a preserved-domain counterexample to C1.

This application uses the existing distinction in [HUIGEN §40](HUIGEN-SELF-GROUND-AUDIT.md#40-affective-disclosure-and-the-badness-of-undergoing): correcting a represented bodily condition and changing the actual experience are different possible changes within one formation. They are not presumed to be independently manipulable in every case. The source comparison is new here; the target-retention criterion and the contrasting cases are inherited. No new clinical result, realization mechanism, ethical theorem or successful C1 derivation is claimed.

**Result and next bridge.** The backward derivation fails at a specified dependence. The affirmative account remains the proposed identity between actual unwanted undergoing and adversity for the life undergoing it, with its existing explanatory support and restricted scope. The newly examined alternative does not yet establish or defeat that identity. A substantive next advance must explain why the independently identified mode constitutes prudential adversity, or defend an account preserving that mode while denying precisely that relation. A mere denial of additional whole-life loss, practical authority or independent token value would not by itself decide this question. A genuine misdescription would require revising the domain rather than expanding it to evade the challenge.

The significance integral continues to express downstream differences conditional on an adequate appraisal of realizations. It cannot discharge this ethical dependence by accumulating it through time. Neither C1 nor the practical bridge C2 has acquired a new foundational assumption or proof in this audit.

**Internal review:** the argument counterreview accepted the exact addition at this scope. The primary-source reviewer accepted its fidelity and requested that our assessment be labeled separately from the source synopsis; that repair is applied. These are AI research reviews, not independent empirical validation. [Owned additions and file checks](ADVERSITY-GROUND-AUDIT-CHECKS.json) record the integration boundary.

## Massin: an identity with a different bearer

6 October 2026. Olivier Massin, “Bad by Nature: An Axiological Theory of Pain,” chapter 27 in Jennifer Corns (ed.), *The Routledge Handbook of Philosophy of Pain* (Routledge, 2017), pp. 321–333, [institutional PDF](https://libra.unine.ch/bitstreams/e4bddcb2-d744-4a48-9f16-19ca4aeae005/download), [publisher metadata](https://www.routledge.com/The-Routledge-Handbook-of-Philosophy-of-Pain-1st-Edition/Corns/p/book/9781315742205). Link-only reading; no imported original or preservation hash.

**Source synopsis:** the account identifies disagreeableness with final, personal, pro tanto badness of bodily episodes. Its initial motivations concern phenomenological unity and the heterogeneity of pain. Section 6 distinguishes such pain from suffering as an affective response and permits genuine suffering of an apparent bodily pain.

**Our assessment:** the chapter does not thereby establish the local bad-for quality of undergoing that response. Its identity cannot simply be transferred to a different bearer.

**Access:** the source contributor read complete main §§1–6, printed pp. 321–330, and notes 1–7 on p. 331 through extracted PDF text. Root inspected selected passages in §§1–2 and §§4–6; the counterreviewer read complete §6 with earlier contextual passages and relevant notes. No figure facsimile or cited clinical evidence was independently checked. Our [backward audit](CONSTITUTIVE-SIGNIFICANCE-ARGUMENT.md#9-backward-audit-the-adversity-assumed-in-correcting-concern) distinguishes this new comparator from its inherited test and unsuccessful grounding route.

**Backward grounding audit, 6 October 2026:** [argument §9](CONSTITUTIVE-SIGNIFICANCE-ARGUMENT.md#9-backward-audit-the-adversity-assumed-in-correcting-concern) records a failed inference from correcting concern back to its assumed adverse ground. The [new source comparison](AFFECTIVE-REALIZATION-SOURCES.md#massin-an-identity-with-a-different-bearer) retains its distinct target and reading limits. The target-preservation criterion is inherited; this round supplies no new ethical theorem or empirical result. The remaining connection is from independently identified unwanted undergoing to local prudential adversity, within the governing whole-process inquiry.

**Backward grounding audit, 6 October 2026:** [the bounded continuation](_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CONSTITUTIVE-SIGNIFICANCE-ARGUMENT.md#9-backward-audit-the-adversity-assumed-in-correcting-concern) records why the proposed correction of concern cannot establish the adversity it already assumes. A new primary comparator applies the inherited requirement to preserve the precise bearer of value; it supplies neither a new proof nor a counterexample. **This audit's unresolved connection:** independently identified unwanted undergoing → local prudential adversity. This supports whole-process grounding without making richer judgments about attitudes a prerequisite for the ethical minimum. Existing formal assumptions remain unchanged.

**Checking the ground used to correct concern, 6 October 2026:** [the backward audit](../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CONSTITUTIVE-SIGNIFICANCE-ARGUMENT.md#9-backward-audit-the-adversity-assumed-in-correcting-concern) rules out recycling an assumed adversity as its own justification. The actual unwanted undergoing remains a differentiated realization to explain within the whole. A source comparison preserves the identity claim's precise target; the unresolved ethical connection has not become a Lean axiom or a completed derivation.

The [backward audit](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CONSTITUTIVE-SIGNIFICANCE-ARGUMENT.md#9-backward-audit-the-adversity-assumed-in-correcting-concern) records a failed route to the starting value: the proposed defect in welcoming adversity already relies on that adversity. It cannot justify its own input. Actual unwanted undergoing remains the candidate realization to explain; neither an attitude toward it nor its accumulated future significance supplies the missing justification. This is an unresolved explanatory connection within the whole account, not evidence that value must enter from outside generation.
